text: I must say that I'm becoming more and more skeptical when you (Steve) benchmark and review graphics cards on this channel, since to even mention DLSS vs FSR and apparently placing them in the same bracket against each other, with room for some kind of discussion and comparing them on equal grounds and that that being the reason to not inform your viewers on a game to game basis?? The technologies aren't comparable at the moment. Comparing NIS and FSR would be another matter entirely and there we can compare and discuss them on equal terms. FSR really isn't even slightly comparable to DLSS since they are completely different technologies where DLSS comes very very high on top of FSR. DLSS is an actual mind blowing feature that gives almost equal or better quality compared to native even on "performance" quality level in ALL games AND giving you more fps at the same time, while FSR is an upscaler comparable to a 10-15 year old TV doing what it can to upscale SDR to 4k with honestly just terrible results in picture quality! I look forward to FSR 2.0 but that's not here at this moment, and when it comes out it will still be years behind Nvidia. Just stating facts here so don't go fanboy slamming me please since as I have said FSR in the state at this moment and DLSS are not even slightly comparable since they, once again, aren't equal technologies at THIS point in time. DLSS is a big reason to choose Nvidia graphics cards atm and I haven't even mentioned the insanely large gap when it comes to Ray Tracing which is for me an even bigger + since I'm having a hard time playing games that dont utilize at least one of the ray traced capabilities. Just play Metro Exodus Enhanced in 120 fps with everything on extreme using DLSS and ALL ray traced features absolutely blows your mind completely and utterly! I don't understand the reasoning here at all to be fair? To only mention that DLSS "MIGHT" be beneficial when it comes to Fortnite is an absolute a joke. All Games supporting DLSS is years ahead of what AMD offers at this time and that should be fairly stated as a quite substantial + in 3080's ballpark in my opinion having used them both for years on LG OLED 65 inch and a 48 inch 4k TV , while always sitting very close and inspecting the differences and they are quite substantial to say the least! Turn on 4k FSR in performance mode and compare 4k DLSS performance mode and the difference is like not having your glasses on with FSR and then putting ON your glasses with DLSS. If you havent seen and used both technologies then you just dont understand that its not even comparable. DLSS is probably the single best evolution in gaming in the history of gaming and I bought my first gaming PC in 1998.

text:
There are two sensible cases to buy a new gpu right now. 
1- You are on Igpu or you are running a really old gpu, older than even an rx 480-470 or gtx 1060-1050ti. In that case these cards are relatively okay for 1080p gaming still and you can still enjoy mid-high quality gaming. Waiting like 4-5 months until new generation gpu releases would make the best sense so buying anything right now is literally a waste of money unless you are using your gpu to make money via 3d rendering etc.
2- Your gpu is broken, it no longer works, therefore you need a display out. Buy a cheap gt 1030 for like $100 or something to get your display out. Play your games at low quality settings until new gpu's are released because either way the gpu prices will continue to drop due to scalper bubble started to blow up. Because it is better to pay $100 now and $800 later than paying $1500 now. I'd rather get a mid-range next gen gpu rather than high-end rtx 30 series or rx 6000 series card. Cause both will probably offer the same amount of performance and next gen will have less power consumption, future tech support and lower price tag. If you're an enthusiast it doesn't make sense to buy a top and gpu right now either, buy the next gen top end gpu instead.

text:
Great stuff, and as a happy 6800XT owner I'd agree that the 3080 12GB has an edge if prices are very close. At this price point, if you say "I don't care about raytracing" then you're wasting money. Unless playing at 4K or very high-frequency displays, but I have the feeling that those scenarios are mostly relevant for benchmarking; I don't know any gamer that will trade 1440p/max-settings/high-fps for 4K, given that even halo GPUs can't do it all at 4K for modern AAA games. With DLSS you can of course do upsampled 4K at a very small cost in quality, but frankly, even without FSR, many AAA games have TSAA that's almost as good.

Also worth noting, Radeon's Infinity Cache tradeoff is great mostly for lower to midrange SKUs. AMD consistently beats NVidia at 1080p and ties at 1440p on raster games. But if you're buying the top-shelf SKU, you're not planning to play at a lowly 1080p. Even with my 6800XT, I never encountered a game that forced me to step down from 1440p to 1080p, even with RT. So the advantage at lower res is irrelevant, AMD should have used a fatter VRAM bus and TDP be damned since NVidia doesn't care about that and apparently most gamers don't care either.

text:
How come there are barely any RT benchmarks when RT is coming in almost all new titles(or being patched in)?, I'm glad that Exodus enhanced edition was tested so people can at least see the massive performance difference that's going to emerge in most new titles going forward. It's almost like it was deliberately left out as always.

The updated HUB methodology; no longer test games maxed out, but change settings on a per game basis to find ones that fit their viewpoint and then test accordingly. You're on a deep slippery slope that leads to invalid test results and a lack of trust. E.G Why was RT on for F1 2021 but not Far Cry 6? Both have extremely limited RT implementations that favour AMD, with the more limited one being F1 2021 which was included, but Far Cry 6 was benchmarked without it, so not truly being maxed out, the most logical conclusion is that F1 2021 favoured AMD, Far Cry 6's result was less favourable so was left out.

Dying Light 2, Far Cry 6 and Cyberpunk 2077 all tested at far far below max settings, in situations that massively favour the AMD card. The impartial testing is so clear it boggles the mind. That said I'm sure we will see a reversion to the normal methods of testing when AMD steps up their RT performance next gen.

It still boggles the mind that sites like this think most people want to spend over £$1000+ on a card and then not max out their games, it used to be a given and would be tested as such, but now simply because a setting has RT in the name it is not tested. Was Doom Eternal left out because after the limited RT patch AMD looses badly in it? How can any of this really be trusted as a neutral source.

Really don't care if you reply to this, but I hope you can provide content that actually reflects the current situation rather than what you want the situation to be.

text:
I would say it is pointless to even look at 3080, because as bad value as 3080Ti is, it is still better card and it is cheaper in most countries and especially on second hand market. I think this is something to do with 3080Ti being mining limited and 3080 unlimited. As result for example in UK 3080Ti sells for £1300, which is close to RRP, whereas 3080 is like £1500-£1600 and that makes no sense. I personally bought both 3080Ti and 6900XT back in October, as it happens both auctions were ending 2 seconds apart and I just won't both of them. Paid £1150 for 3080Ti and £1172 for 6900XT. In my personal testing 3080Ti was ~2% faster on average compared to 6900XT, which is in line with this testing where 6900XT is on average few % faster than 3080. Meaning 3080Ti is maybe 4% faster than 3080, again in line with previous tests and this is why I said that buying 3080 just doesn't make sense, it is 4% slower and costs £300 more in current market. I personally kept 6900XT, the reason was simple - my 3080Ti is FE and my 6900XT is Asus Strix OC LC, just generally much higher end card with water cooling and OC, absolutely quiet and hardly ever reaches even 40C, besides it runs just fine on 850W PSU, in other hand 3080Ti FE was loud and hot (like 98C under load) and it would trip OCP on 850W PSU, requiring me to use 1500W PSU for testing (it would probably run on 1200W). And secondly, I can resell 3080Ti for said £1300-£1350, whereas 6900XT sells at best for £1250 despite being nearly matching performance card.
In summary, if we look at RRP prices 3080 would be best value, followed by 6900XT and 3080Ti would be kind of horrible, but when we look at real life prices, then 6900XT is actually the cheapest, followed by 3080Ti and 3080 is just horrible deal all around.

@AndrewTSq  The fact that there are no reference 3080s available isn't exactly a mark in NVIDIA's favor here.  Steve used stock clocks because it's the fairest way to compare apples to apples. text:
@HalenShredder   StealthHunter explained the inconsistent Destiny framerates perfectly. 
HU and GN used GTA in most benchmarks, even to this date. This is the first time I’ve NOT seen GTA on the list. 
I’m obviously aware most people play GTA Online (with its horrible framerates, depending on the lobby’s activity). As I tried to explain before: you can’t benchmark ‘online-only’ games. Too many variables. Check your CPU usage in a solo lobby versus a regular online lobby. 
R6S is a consistent game. For Destiny, even your class setup matters. I’d imagine a Hunter would get more FPS than a Warlock or Titan, for example. 
What’s the use in benchmarking games where you can’t reproduce the exact same testing conditions?
Benchmarking ANY game (when testing conditions can be reproduced) is useful, just for the sheer data it provides. If I’d run the exact same benchmarks on a system with the exact same specs, I’d still see different numbers based on background activity, a multi-monitor setup, effective SSD speed et cetera. 
I don’t play 45ish games on this list, would you say it’s ‘wasted effort’ on HU’s part because they don’t benchmark the games you want to see?

No, you do not get different FPS depending on what class you're playing, at least certainly not the way you're describing. I don't know where you imagined that.

And to the ultimate point, it doesn't even really matter what specific games are used. The point of all those games on the list isn't to feature the one you want to see, or the games that you play. It's just to provide a general guide to the average performance you can expect from the GPU in scenarios where it's not bottlenecked when compared to other GPUs, and that's it. It's not a "here's how much FPS you can expect in these games" guide. Every reviewer uses a flagship CPU for their test system, and obviously most people don't have a 5950X or 12900k or whatever, so your system is obviously not represented in any of these reviews. The bigger the sample size, the better, and using more modern titles is a better pool to pull from than older games, even if the older game is still popular. If you want something like that, go watch a specific game benchmark video, there's plenty of them

Lastly, it's a new expansion today, with a replayable campaign, so theoretically that provides a good benchmarking scenario.

text: @dirk_valentine  You're not wrong, but here's my thought. The 3060ti is really intended to be a premium 1080p card. Sure, it can play some games in 1440p or even 4K, but it shows the best performance at 1080p, without being absolutely ridiculous. For the lifetime of the card, 5-6 years or 2 GPU generations, 4K will probably not become the standard for monitors. While it IS tracking in that direction, and 1440p is being bypassed by retailers for the most part, the 3060ti simply can't do 4K reliably right now in modern games, and 8gb is still plenty for 1080p. Right now the SHS only shows 4K monitors making up less than 2% of the market (which, while certainly not all PC users, is still a sizable chunk). Even if you assume that's reflective of the overall trend, and even if you make the crazy jump that 4K monitors become 8x more popular in the next 4.5 years... you're still looking at that only being roughly 16% of the market. The 4060 will probably also be a 1080p card and, frankly, I think the 5060 might be best for 1440p, given the trends. By then, surely the cards will have 12gb, or running on GDDR7.
